provenance: 0contract EVM DeFi/bridge archetype catalog, grounded in rekt.news post-mortems + public CVEs/advisories, curated 2026-07-08

archetypes.name: Classic reentrancy — external call before state settlement
archetypes.pattern: A withdraw/redeem path sends ETH or calls an ERC20/ERC777/ERC721 hook BEFORE zeroing the caller's internal balance/shares, so the callee re-enters the same function and drains the pool while the pre-decrement balance still reads full.
archetypes.detection_signature: An external value-moving call (`.call{value:}`, `token.transfer`, `_safeMint`, ERC777 `tokensReceived`) followed LATER in the same function by the state write (`balances[msg.sender] = 0`, `shares -= amount`). No `nonReentrant` and not Checks-Effects-Interactions ordered.

archetypes.name: Read-only reentrancy — stale view read mid-callback
archetypes.pattern: A `view` (get_virtual_price, getReserves, share price) is read by a THIRD contract while a mid-transaction callback has left the source pool's invariant temporarily broken, yielding a manipulated price to the consumer even though the source contract itself has a nonReentrant guard.
archetypes.detection_signature: A price/share `view` consumed cross-contract, whose source updates balances and fires an external callback (remove_liquidity ETH send) non-atomically. The guard protects state-changing entrypoints but NOT the view.

archetypes.name: Unprotected initializer / init front-run (uninitialized proxy)
archetypes.pattern: A proxy or implementation exposes `initialize()` without an effective one-time guard or with the implementation left uninitialized, so an attacker calls it first to set themselves as owner (or initializes + selfdestructs a UUPS impl to brick the proxy).
archetypes.detection_signature: `initialize()` with a missing/loose `initializer` modifier, or a UUPS/`_authorizeUpgrade` implementation whose constructor omits `_disableInitializers()`. `_setOwner(msg.sender)` reachable pre-ownership.
grounding: Wormhole uninitialized proxy bugfix 2022 ($10M Immunefi bounty)

archetypes.name: Missing access control on privileged / value-moving function
archetypes.pattern: A state-changing or fund-moving function (mint, setOwner, withdrawAll, setImplementation, addMinter) has no `onlyOwner`/`onlyRole` gate, or gates on `tx.origin`, so any address can invoke the admin action.
archetypes.detection_signature: `external`/`public` function that transfers value, mints, or mutates ownership/roles with NO modifier and no `require(msg.sender == owner)`; or an auth check on `tx.origin`.

archetypes.name: Spot-price oracle manipulation via flash loan
archetypes.pattern: Collateral/borrow value is priced from an AMM SPOT read (getReserves / balanceOf(pool) / getAmountOut) within one transaction; attacker flash-loans, skews the pool, borrows or liquidates against the false price, then repays.
archetypes.detection_signature: `getReserves`/`getAmountOut`/pool `balanceOf` feeding a `getPrice`/collateral-value calc, with no TWAP and no independent oracle. Reachable alongside a flash-loan callback.

archetypes.name: Oracle price manipulation via lending-market / vault donation
archetypes.pattern: An empty or thin market lets an attacker manipulate the exchange rate by self-borrowing/self-liquidating or donating assets to inflate the per-share price, then extracting more than deposited (the Euler donation + self-liquidation class).
archetypes.detection_signature: Exchange rate = cash+borrows / totalSupply with no floor on totalSupply and a `donateToReserves`/direct-transfer path that moves `totalAssets` without minting shares; self-liquidation not blocked.

archetypes.name: First-depositor / ERC4626 share-inflation via donation
archetypes.pattern: First depositor mints 1 wei of shares, then transfers assets directly into the vault to inflate totalAssets, so the next depositor's `assets * totalSupply / totalAssets` rounds to zero shares and their deposit is captured by the attacker.
archetypes.detection_signature: `convertToShares` = `assets * totalSupply / totalAssets` with no virtual-shares/dead-shares offset and no minimum first deposit; `totalAssets()` reads live `balanceOf` (donation-inflatable).

archetypes.name: Rounding / precision loss captured by attacker
archetypes.pattern: Division truncates in the attacker's favor (round-down owed, round-up credited) or divide-before-multiply loses precision, letting repeated small operations skim value or mint free shares.
archetypes.detection_signature: `a / b * c` (divide before multiply), rounding that credits the user (`ceil` on mint, `floor` on burn), or fee math with no minimum. Missing `mulDiv` with correct rounding direction.
grounding: numerous audit 'rounding in favor of protocol' findings

archetypes.name: Signature replay — missing nonce / deadline
archetypes.pattern: A signature-authorized action does not consume a per-signer nonce (or checks it after the effect), so the same signature is replayed to repeat a withdrawal/claim/approval.
archetypes.detection_signature: `ecrecover`/`_hashTypedDataV4` verifying a signed message with no `nonces[signer]++` before the action, or a `usedSignatures` map never set.

archetypes.name: EIP-712 domain reuse — cross-chain / cross-deploy signature replay
archetypes.pattern: The domain separator omits `block.chainid` and/or `address(this)`, so a signature valid on one chain or one deployment is replayable on a fork/other chain/redeployed contract.
archetypes.detection_signature: `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR` computed once in the constructor (cached across a fork) or without `chainid`/`verifyingContract` in the type hash; no re-derivation when `block.chainid` changes.

archetypes.name: Cross-chain: uninitialized / zero trusted-root accepted
archetypes.pattern: The bridge's message-verification treats an uninitialized (zero) committed root as valid, so any message proves against the default-empty mapping and anyone forges withdrawals of bridged value.
archetypes.detection_signature: `acceptableRoot(0x00) == true` or a `confirmAt`/`roots` mapping whose default zero value passes the proof check; `process()` gated only by `acceptableRoot` on an attacker-supplied root.
grounding: Nomad Bridge 2022 ($190M, zero-root after routine init)

archetypes.name: Cross-chain: missing source-address / source-chain / endpoint binding
archetypes.pattern: An inbound handler (`lzReceive`, `ccipReceive`, `_execute`, `handle`) does not verify msg.sender is the trusted endpoint AND the (srcChainId, srcAddress) trusted remote, so a forged call mints/releases value on the destination.
archetypes.detection_signature: `lzReceive`/`ccipReceive` with no `require(msg.sender == endpoint)` or no `require(trustedRemote[srcChainId] == srcAddress)`; sender/chain fields read but not enforced.
grounding: cross-chain 'anyone can call receive' audit findings

archetypes.name: Cross-chain: message replay — no per-message nonce
archetypes.pattern: A delivered cross-chain message (or its VAA/leaf/messageHash) can be re-submitted because no per-message nonce or processed-set is enforced, replaying a mint/withdraw multiple times.
archetypes.detection_signature: Message handler that credits value keyed by (chain, nonce) or a `messageHash` with no `processed[hash] = true` guard set before the effect; Wormhole VAA hash not recorded as consumed.

archetypes.name: Cross-chain: broken guardian/signature verification (VAA)
archetypes.pattern: Signature/guardian-set verification of a bridge attestation is bypassable — a spoofed or unchecked signer set lets a forged VAA mint wrapped assets without a real deposit.
archetypes.detection_signature: `parseAndVerifyVM`/guardian-set check missing or verifying against an attacker-influenceable set; the classic `verify_signatures` shortcut that accepts a sysvar/instruction-spoofed signer set.

archetypes.name: Delegatecall storage-layout collision
archetypes.pattern: A `delegatecall` into a library/implementation whose storage layout differs from the caller's, so a write at slot N in the callee clobbers an unrelated caller variable (owner, impl pointer, balance).
archetypes.detection_signature: `delegatecall` to an impl whose declared state variables do not align slot-for-slot with the proxy's (no `__gap`, reordered vars across an upgrade), or unstructured-storage slots that overlap.

archetypes.name: Arbitrary delegatecall / call to attacker-controlled target
archetypes.pattern: A function forwards a caller-supplied `target` and `data` into `delegatecall`/`call`, letting the attacker execute arbitrary code in the contract's context (drain approvals, set owner) — often combined with `msg.value` reuse in a payable multicall.
archetypes.detection_signature: `target.delegatecall(data)` / `target.call(data)` where `target` is a function parameter with no allowlist; `payable` multicall looping over calls that each read `msg.value`.

archetypes.name: Unchecked external-call / transfer return value
archetypes.pattern: A low-level `call`/`send` or a bare ERC20 `transfer`/`transferFrom` return is ignored, so a silently-failing (or no-return / false-returning) token lets accounting proceed as if value moved.
archetypes.detection_signature: `token.transfer(...)` as a statement (return not checked) without SafeERC20; `addr.call(...)` / `addr.send(...)` whose `bool success` is discarded.

archetypes.name: Fee-on-transfer / rebasing token accounting desync
archetypes.pattern: The contract credits the requested `amount` on deposit rather than the actual received balance delta, so a fee-on-transfer or rebasing token lets the attacker withdraw more than the pool actually received.
archetypes.detection_signature: `transferFrom(user, this, amount)` followed by `balances[user] += amount` (uses the requested amount, not `balanceAfter - balanceBefore`); no double-entry-point / rebasing guard.

archetypes.name: Flash-loan governance takeover
archetypes.pattern: Voting power is read from a live token balance (not a historical snapshot), so an attacker flash-loans governance tokens, passes a malicious proposal in one transaction, and drains the treasury.
archetypes.detection_signature: `getVotes`/quorum using `balanceOf`/current supply instead of a past-block snapshot (`getPastVotes`/checkpoints); proposal execution reachable in the same tx as vote casting.

archetypes.name: Missing slippage / deadline — sandwichable swap
archetypes.pattern: A swap/deposit/withdraw executes with `minAmountOut = 0` (or an attacker-suppliable bound) and/or `deadline = block.timestamp`, so a searcher sandwiches the transaction and skims the difference.
archetypes.detection_signature: `swapExactTokensForTokens(..., 0, ..., block.timestamp)` or an internal swap with no caller-supplied min-out; auto-computed min-out from the same manipulable pool.

archetypes.name: Unbounded-loop / push-payment DoS (griefing)
archetypes.pattern: A function loops over an attacker-growable array or push-pays a list of recipients, so one reverting recipient or a large array pushes gas past the block limit and permanently bricks the function.
archetypes.detection_signature: `for` over `holders`/`queue`/per-user array with no bound; a payout loop that reverts wholesale if one `transfer` fails (favor pull-payments).

archetypes.name: On-chain randomness from block values
archetypes.pattern: Randomness is derived from `block.timestamp`/`blockhash`/`prevrandao`, which a validator or a same-block contract can predict/influence to win the lottery or mint the rare NFT.
archetypes.detection_signature: `keccak256(abi.encodePacked(block.timestamp, block.difficulty, ...))` used as a winning/selection seed; no commit-reveal or VRF.
